title: ioctl_key_generate: does not validate op.algo is non-empty
description: ioctl_key_generate() forces null-termination on op.algo (op.algo[CRYPTO2DEV_ALGO_MAXLEN-1]='\0') but does NOT check if op.algo[0]=='\0' (empty string). It then calls crypto2dev_lookup_algo(op.algo, ...) with an empty string. crypto2dev_lookup_algo() does a strcmp against registered algo names — no registered algo has name '' (empty string), so lookup returns NULL and KEY_GENERATE returns -ENOENT. This is a correct outcome but the wrong error code: -ENOENT means 'no provider for this algo' whereas -EINVAL means 'bad argument'. An empty algo string is clearly a caller error (-EINVAL), not a lookup miss (-ENOENT). Compare ioctl_init() which explicitly checks 'if (op.algo[0] == 0) return -EINVAL' — ioctl_key_generate() lacks this check. Trigger: KEY_GENERATE with algo[0]='\0' → returns -ENOENT instead of -EINVAL.
close_reason: fixed: added if (op.algo[0] == '\0') return -EINVAL after null-termination in ioctl_key_generate
